chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar Bin Yazeed, who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the vessel is coloured (by the residue), drink it.'
ai.seo_question: Is the residue of grape juice (Tala'a) considered pure and permissible to drink?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of consuming *Tala'a* (evaporated grape juice) by using a physical indicator: if the residue has thickened enough to color the vessel (*yakhdi'u al-ina'a*), it is considered pure and fit for drinking. This ruling addresses the juristic debate regarding the transition of grape juice from a non-intoxicant to a potential intoxicant, establishing that the specific consistency of *Tala'a* retains its purity (*tahir*) and does not become *khamr* (wine) unless it ferments further.

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the vessel was coloured (due to the evaporation of the two-thirds of it), so drink it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When two-thirds of juice (grape juice) is evaporated (because of boiling) then you can drink it.’”
